title: Prefill Gambit — Operational Digest and Action Log (2026-11-03)
body:
Meeting: Prefill Gambit sync — 2026-11-03 09:30 PT
Attendees: Ava Martinez (owner), Jonah Reed, Priya Nair, Marco Liu, Riley Chen, Ad-hoc: Tanya (SRE)
Purpose: capture latest kernel+KV prefill experiments, surface anomalies from last 72h, and agree on operational next steps for stabilizing p95 during nightly traffic spikes.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Recent microkernel change (PR 2187) improved batching efficiency but widened latency variance under low-concurrency, causing p95 regressions on a subset of short-sequence requests.
- KV cache prefill hit-rate recovered to 71% after the coalescing tweak but we observed 18% increased eviction churn on GPUs hosting mixed quantized models.
- Two concrete action items: (1) roll a targeted hotfix to the kernel backpressure thresholds (owner: Marco, due 11/05); (2) revert a memory-reclamation heuristic for quantized shards in the prefill path while we debug eviction patterns (owner: Priya, due 11/04).

What we observed
1) Kernel batching behaviour
- Experiment: microkernel scheduling (PR 2187) enabled intra-core cooperative coalescing for small requests. Benchmarks in staging: throughput +6% at high load, median latency unchanged.
- Production effect: p50 stable, p95 increased by ~40ms for 512-token max requests during low concurrency windows (observed 11/01 23:00–11/03 03:00 UTC).
- Hypothesis: cooperative coalescing prolongs head-of-line time for late-arriving short requests when the scheduling quantum hits, creating more jitter for those classes.
- Quick check: toggling the quantum to 2ms reduces p95 but drops throughput for long-seq workloads.

2) KV cache prefill and eviction churn
- Hit-rate: runway tests show prefill hit-rate 71% overall (goal 78%); model-specific variance: generator models hit-rate 83%, chat variants 64%.
- Evictions: eviction rate on GPU-A (mixed 4-bit/8-bit endpoints) increased 18% after memory-reclamation heuristic (JIRA-OPS-1124). Evictions cluster during burst windows => observed increased regenerations and re-prefill costs.
- Hypothesis: reclamation is too aggressive for shards that see intermittent reuse; when reclaimed and then needed the cost to re-prefill exceeds the time saved.

3) Batching jitter and queueing
- Observed intermittent queue head shuffling when reorderer and sampler interact under cross-tenant traffic. Metrics: queue-size variance up 2.1x in peak 4-hour windows; queue reorder events correlate with p95 spikes.
- Sampler tweak in staging lowered overall queue waits but increased starved batch formation for a tiny slice of low-token requests.

Operational incidents and mitigations (last 72h)
- 2026-11-02 01:14 UTC: elevated p95 for hosted-api region-us-west-2. Triage found increased evictions on nodes running mixed quantized models. Temporary mitigation: pinned eviction disable for those nodes (manual flag) until hotfix applied.
- 2026-11-02 04:30 UTC: oncall rotated sampling config (reverted recent sampler gating) to reduce jitter — small throughput regression but p95 recovered.

Decisions made in sync
- Do not roll PR 2187 to fleet until hotfix for backpressure scheduling is in place. Rationale: throughput gains don't justify the observed p95 instability for low-concurrency short requests.
- Re-enable conservative prefill retention for quantized shards while we gather eviction telemetry and a trace-driven eviction policy is designed.
- SRE to add temporary sampling/priority override for tenant-critical routes (config flag: sampling.priority_override).

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Marco Liu: implement kernel backpressure hotfix (lower default scheduling quantum when queue variance > threshold; safe config flag) — due 2026-11-05 — JIRA-SRV-3407.
- Priya Nair: revert aggressive memory-reclamation heuristic for quantized prefill path; add telemetry for reclaimed-shard re-prefill events — due 2026-11-04 — linked PR to follow.
- Jonah Reed: run 48h staging flood test with mixed short/long sequences to measure tradeoffs between throughput and p95 for updated kernel config; collect per-model p95 and KV hit-rate slices — start 2026-11-04, report 2026-11-06.
- Riley Chen: update prefill playbook with temporary rollback steps and eviction-detection runbook (include checklist for manual disable flag) — due 2026-11-05.
- Ava Martinez: schedule follow-up deep-dive (60m) to review telemetry and traces from reverted heuristic and kernel hotfix once both are in staging — meeting 2026-11-06 09:30 PT.

Open questions / investigations
- Which model characteristics (prompt templates, token distribution, system messages) are most correlated with the low hit-rate chat variants? Action: Jonah to synthesize sample prompt distribution and forward to model-onboarding.
- Is eviction churn driven by cross-tenant noisy neighbors or by internal memory compaction timing? Need a trace that links eviction event to last-access timestamp and tenant-id. Action: Priya to add per-shard last-access label and record eviction cause.
- Can we design a cheap predictive retention heuristic: retain shards with usage > X over last Y minutes rather than LRU-only? Brainstorm scheduled on 2026-11-07; invitees: eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml.

Notes from quick profiling (attached findings)
- Kernel timeline sample (short request): shows waiting 1.6–2.6ms in coalesce gate; additional scheduling jitter ~18–45ms when quantum collides with arrival pattern.
- Prefill memory graph: 6% of shards dominate 52% of re-prefill cost; these are primarily chat-context shards used by a 2 large enterprise tenants.

Temporary checklist for oncall (copy into runbook)
1) If p95 spike seen: check eviction rate dashboard (panel: prefill.evictions/node).
2) If evictions elevated and correlated with target tenant: toggle eviction_disable flag for affected nodes, escalate to eng-serving-runtime.
3) If queue-reorder events increase: enable sampling.priority_override for critical routes; coordinate with SRE to monitor throughput impact.
4) Collect traces for 10 affected requests (trace ids) and attach to JIRA ticket.

Planned experiments next sprint (brief)
- Predictive-retention A/B (small cohort): keep top-K frequently used shards pinned vs LRU baseline. Measure re-prefill cost, memory headroom, hit-rate. Owner: Priya.
- Adaptive quantum: dynamic per-core quantum based on queue variance instead of static config. Owner: Marco + Jonah.
- Per-model prefill tuning: prioritize chat variants with lower baseline hit-rate for eager prefill. Owner: Applied ML / Jonah.

Concluding notes
We have a clear path: small hotfixes + conservative rollback on reclamation to restore p95 SLAs, while we gather higher-fidelity telemetry to design a predictive retention policy. The immediate focus is to ship Marco's backpressure fix and Priya's reclamation revert into staging, run the 48h flood, and reconvene with traces on 11/06.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2187 (microkernel coalescing)
- Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/Prefill+Playbook
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1124 (eviction heuristic), JIRA-SRV-3407 (kernel scheduling hotfix)
- Slack channel: #eng-serving-runtime (use thread pref: "prefill-gambit")

Document notes: informal operational digest intended for eng-serving-runtime and SRE. Update status to in_review when hotfix PRs are green in staging.
